q: On which planet is Tress of the Emerald Sea set?
explain: Lumar is a world of spore oceans fed by twelve moons, each hosting an aether.

q: What does Tress love to collect at the start of her story?
explain: Tress treasures her cups for the stories each one seems to tell.
source: Tress of the Emerald Sea, ch. 1

q: What kind of animal is Huck, Tress's talking companion?
explain: Huck is a cursed talking rat who secretly spies for the Sorceress.

q: Who is Charlie, the young man Tress sets out to rescue?
explain: The duke sent Charlie away on a voyage, and he ended up a prisoner of the Sorceress.

q: In which sea does the Sorceress hold her domain?
explain: The Sorceress rules the Midnight Sea, where Tress must sail to rescue Charlie.

q: What happens when verdant spores come into contact with water?
explain: Sailors use verdant vines as fuses or to entangle opponents.

q: Which spores release a burst of air when wet, making them ideal for firing cannons?
explain: Zephyr spores fall on the Sapphire Sea and are used to propel cannonballs.

q: What is Fort's position aboard the Crow's Song?
explain: Fort is deaf and communicates through a Nalthian board.

q: What does Dr. Ulaam, the Crow's Song's surgeon, ask for as payment?
explain: Hoid claims Ulaam is the best doctor he has ever met, despite his odd fee.

q: Who does the crew elect as captain after Crow is removed?
explain: Tress trades Crow to the dragon Xisis, and the grateful crew chooses her to lead.

q: What is the name of the new ship Tress and her crew buy at the end of the story?
explain: Pardoned by the king, the crew sell the Crow's Song and buy the Two Cups, with Charlie aboard as valet, storyteller and musician.
source: Tress of the Emerald Sea; Coppermind: Two Cups

q: In which of the twelve seas does the dragon Xisis make his home?
explain: Xisis is a dragon originally from Yolen who, for a time, made his home in the Crimson Sea.
source: Tress of the Emerald Sea; Coppermind: Xisis

q: On which planet do Yumi and Painter live?
explain: Komashi is home both to Yumi's yoki-hijo traditions and to Painter's city of Kilahito.

q: What does Yumi stack into delicate towers to summon spirits?
explain: The spirits she draws grant blessings to the villagers of her land.

q: What does Painter hunt and capture with his brush and ink?
explain: Nightmares seep out of the shroud, and painters trap them by painting them into harmless images.

q: What sacred title does Yumi hold among her people?
explain: A yoki-hijo summons spirits for her people at great cost to her own freedom.

q: What is Painter's real name?
explain: Nikaro usually goes by Painter, after his job as a nightmare painter.

q: What hangs permanently over the city of Kilahito?
explain: Under the shroud Kilahito lives in constant darkness, lit by glowing hion lines.

q: In which two colors do Kilahito's hion lines glow?
explain: Hion lines run through the city, providing both light and power.

q: Who is Yumi's strict guardian and attendant?
explain: Liyun oversees Yumi's rigid daily rituals as a yoki-hijo.

q: Which of these characters is a fellow nightmare painter in Kilahito?
explain: Painter meets Akane and Tojin on patrol at the city's western edge.
source: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter, ch. 1

q: What is Masaka, who works as a nightmare painter, secretly?
explain: Masaka, whose Sleepless name is Chinikdakordich, poses as an ordinary nightmare painter in Kilahito.
source: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter; Coppermind: Masaka

q: Which Shard Splintered herself on Komashi?
explain: The remnants of Virtuosity's power shaped the strange Investiture of Komashi.

q: On which planet is The Sunlit Man set?
explain: Canticle is a world scorched by a deadly, Invested sun.

q: Why must the cities of Canticle keep constantly moving?
explain: Anyone caught in Canticle's direct sunlight is burned to ash.

q: In The Sunlit Man, what is Rebeke riding when Nomad latches on to it and is dragged away with her?
explain: Nomad hurls a chain onto Rebeke's departing hovercycle, and the sunlight starts to burn him as he is dragged away.

q: By what name was Nomad known when he lived on Roshar?
explain: Sigzil was a member of Bridge Four before becoming the worldhopping Nomad.

q: Which group hunts Nomad from world to world?
explain: Nomad keeps Skipping between planets to stay ahead of the Night Brigade.

q: Which tyrant rules the planet where The Sunlit Man is set?
explain: The Cinder King commands the Charred, people enslaved by a corrupted sunheart driven into their chests.

q: What does Nomad's Torment make him unable to do?
explain: The Torment stops him from causing harm even in self-defense.

q: What is the cause of Nomad's Torment?
explain: Holding a Dawnshard leaves a lasting mark on whoever carried it.

q: What kind of being is Auxiliary, Nomad's talking companion?
explain: Aux was nearly consumed by the Dawnshard Nomad once held and survives as a voice in Nomad's head.

q: On which planet is White Sand set?
explain: Taldain is tidally locked, split into an eternal Dayside and Darkside.

q: What do Sand Masters expend from their own bodies to control sand?
explain: Overusing sand mastery can dangerously dehydrate a Sand Master.

q: Who is Kenton's father, the powerful Lord Mastrell?
explain: Praxton dies fighting the Kerztians, his final attack burying Kenton in sand.

q: What color does white sand turn after a Sand Master uses it?
explain: Spent sand turns white again after about four hours in Dayside's sunlight.

q: What is distinctive about Taldain's Darkside?
a: It always faces a dim star
explain: Khriss hails from Darkside, which faces a white dwarf hidden behind a particle ring.

q: What is the name of the order of Sand Masters that Kenton belongs to?
explain: Kenton eventually becomes Lord Mastrell, leader of the Diem.

q: Which Shard Invests Taldain through its blazing larger star?
explain: Taldain orbits a blue-white supergiant paired with a dim white dwarf.
source: Arcanum Unbounded, Taldain system essay; Coppermind: Taldain system

q: On which planet is Sixth of the Dusk set?
explain: First of the Sun is an ocean world dotted with deadly islands.

q: What are the talent-granting birds of First of the Sun called?
explain: Young Aviar must visit the island of Patji to gain their talents.

q: What is Dusk's profession?
explain: Dusk traps Aviar on Patji, as was the tradition among his people.

q: Patji, the largest island of the Pantheon, is often called what?
explain: Dusk and his people treat the deadly island of Patji with wary reverence, as a stern father.

q: What does Dusk's Aviar Sak show him?
explain: Sak's corpse visions warn Dusk of danger ahead; her talent was unknown among Aviar before her.

q: What talent does Dusk's Aviar Kokerlii grant him?
explain: On Patji, many predators hunt by sensing minds, so Kokerlii is vital.

q: On which planet do the Forests of Hell grow?
explain: The Forests of Hell are haunted by shades, the spirits of the dead.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell

q: What does Silence Montane run in the Forests of Hell?
explain: Silence runs the waystop with her daughter, William Ann.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell

q: Which metal can destroy the shades of Threnody?
explain: Shades grow enraged if someone lights a fire, runs at night or sheds blood.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell

q: Under what secret identity does Silence hunt bounties?
explain: Silence uses the bounties she collects to keep her waystop out of debt.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell

q: What became of Silence's grandmother after she was killed?
a: Her shade is bound in a shrine
wrong: She was buried in the Homeland
She was burned on a pyre
explain: Silence trapped the shade of her strict grandmother in the waystop's shrine, and later unleashes it on the tax collector.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell; Coppermind: Silence's grandmother

q: What job does Tress take on aboard the Crow's Song?
explain: As the ship's sprouter, Tress handles the aether spores the crew uses to fight and to repair the ship.
source: Tress of the Emerald Sea; Coppermind: Ulaam

q: What is Dr. Ulaam, the Crow's Song's surgeon, secretly?
explain: Ulaam is a kandra from Scadrial working as the ship's surgeon.
source: Tress of the Emerald Sea; Coppermind: Ulaam

q: Why did Ann originally sign on to the Crow's Song as its carpenter?
a: To avoid being drafted into the king's army
wrong: To pay off her family's debts
To search for a lost brother
explain: Ann later volunteered to serve as the ship's assistant cannonmaster.
source: Tress of the Emerald Sea; Coppermind: Ann

q: What do roseite spores do when they touch water?
explain: Sprouters use roseite crystal to patch damaged hulls.
source: Tress of the Emerald Sea; Coppermind: Aether spores

q: What lowly position does Hoid hold aboard the Crow's Song?
explain: Hoid, the book's narrator, mops the Crow's Song's decks while under the Sorceress's curse.

q: What did the father machine turn most of Torio's people into?
explain: Built to harvest Investiture from the hijo, the machine created the shroud and held the dead captive as Cognitive Shadows.
source: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter; Coppermind: Father machine

q: What had really been happening to Yumi before she was linked to Painter?
a: She was trapped in a simulation of her old life
wrong: She slept frozen inside a shrine
She was lost in Painter's dreams
She was a spirit bound inside a stone stack
explain: After it killed her, the father machine hid Yumi in a simulation of her former life and patched over her memories to keep her complacent.
source: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter; Coppermind: Yumi

q: In Yumi and the Nightmare Painter, what did Hoid's companion open in Kilahito while he was frozen in time?
explain: The Noodle Pupil was run with the cook Namakudo and later left to Yumi and Painter, who renamed it the Noodle Princess.
source: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter; Coppermind: Noodle Pupil

q: What are the hijo, the spirits that Yumi summons on Komashi?
explain: Hijo live underground and are drawn to thoughts, emotions and art.
source: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter; Coppermind: Hijo

q: Which of these women served as one of Yumi's attendants?
explain: Hwanji, known for humming as she worked, had previously served Dwookim.
source: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter, ch. 2; Coppermind: Hwanji

q: Where do Canticle's sunhearts come from?
a: The Investiture of people who die there
explain: Sunhearts form from people who perish in Canticle's Invested sunlight, and they power the flying cities.

q: Canticle's people descend from settlers who came from which planet?
explain: Canticle's people descend from Threnodite settlers.
source: The Sunlit Man; Coppermind: Cinder King

q: What title does Elegy Salvage receive when the Greater Good chooses her to lead the city of Beacon?
explain: Naming Elegy Beacon's Lodestar ended the practice of sacrificing the city's eldest members.

q: What are Canticle's flying cities, such as Beacon, built from?
explain: The linked ships can be steered as one, kept aloft by sunhearts.

q: How is Elegy Salvage, who comes to lead the city of Beacon, related to Rebeke?
explain: Rebeke and Elegy, along with their brother Divinity, belong to the Salvage family.
source: The Sunlit Man; Coppermind: Elegy Salvage

q: Besides sand mastery, what else uses up the power of Taldain's white sand?
explain: Wet sand loses its power just like sand that has been mastered, until sunlight recharges it.

q: What gives Taldain's Invested sand its white color?
a: A microorganism living on the grains
explain: The organism draws on the light of Taldain's larger sun, which also recharges spent sand.
source: Arcanum Unbounded, The Taldain System; Coppermind: Sand mastery

q: How many Taisha sit on the Taishin, the ruling council of Lossand?
explain: Each Taisha heads one of Lossand's Professions; the Lord Mastrell speaks for the Sand Masters.

q: What did Kenton do during his run of the Mastrell's Path that was thought impossible?
a: Killed the deep sandling that guarded it
wrong: Finished it without using sand mastery
Completed it in a single night
explain: Kenton used his sword to kill the sandling at the heart of the Path, destroying the Path forever.

q: During which event do the Kerztian warrior-priests attack Kenton's order of Sand Masters?
explain: Almost every Sand Master is killed, and Kenton believes he is the only survivor.

q: Which notorious highwayman does Silence hunt to pay off her debts?
explain: Silence tracks Chesterton and his crew through the Forests of Hell.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell; Coppermind: Silence Montane

q: Which tax collector from the forts threatens to claim Silence's waystop?
explain: Theopolis warns Silence that the fort will take her waystop if she does not pay her taxes within a few days.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell, ch. 1

q: Who is the stableman at Silence's waystop?
explain: In the first chapter Silence sends Dob on his break so she can water the horses herself.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell, ch. 1

q: Who is Red Young?
a: A bounty hunter from the forts
explain: Red Young is one of the bounty hunters working out of the forts on Threnody.
source: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell; Coppermind: Red Young

q: According to Khriss's essay, how many continents does Threnody have?
explain: The larger continent was overrun by the Evil, while the smaller, forested one became the Forests of Hell.

q: How do the Eelakin regard the islands of the Pantheon?
wrong: As the tombs of their ancestors
As the property of their king
explain: Each trapper serves as a kind of priest of the island he traps.
source: Sixth of the Dusk; Coppermind: Pantheon

q: What is the trading company's offworld machine meant to do on Patji?
a: Locate all of the island's Aviar
explain: The machine was never meant to run: its offworld makers hoped its technology would hurry the Eelakin's progress so they could get around laws forbidding trade.
source: Sixth of the Dusk; Coppermind: Sixth of the Dusk (character)

q: What actually grants the talented birds of Dusk's world their abilities?
a: A parasite they pick up on the islands
explain: Sak, a mainland bird, only gained her talent after Dusk took her to Patji.
source: Sixth of the Dusk; Coppermind: Aviar

q: Who taught Dusk his profession?
explain: After his uncle died on a trip to Patji, Dusk carried on alone on that island, as tradition demanded.
source: Sixth of the Dusk; Coppermind: Sixth of the Dusk (character)

q: What is a deepwalker?
a: A huge sea predator that hunts by sensing minds
wrong: A diving ship of the Ones Above
explain: A deepwalker wiped out Vathi's scouting team after it camped too close to the beach.
source: Sixth of the Dusk; Coppermind: Deepwalker
